submission.name: PairPort
submission.tagline: Share a live view of your lab setup so a teammate can point, click, and help troubleshoot.
submission.inspiration: We wanted classmates in data and computing labs to be able to get help without crowding around one screen. A shared view with remote input seemed useful for walking through a bug or showing a confusing workflow.
submission.what_it_does: PairPort captures a host's screen and lets a connected viewer send mouse and keyboard input while the host keeps working. We also tried a simple session label so teams could tell which lab task they were looking at, but the full demo did not connect end to end.
submission.how_we_built_it: The prototype uses Python with MSS for screen capture, OpenCV and Pillow for image handling, PySide6 for the desktop interface, and PyAutoGUI for input events. We used Pyngrok while exploring connections and AI coding tools for planning and code suggestions; the capture and input pieces run separately, but we did not get a reliable complete streaming session.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Getting screen frames and remote input to stay responsive at the same time was harder than expected, and the pieces did not come together into a working demo. Generated code also added extra complexity, so we spent time trimming it and narrowing the feature set.
submission.accomplishments: We got isolated screen-capture and input experiments running and learned what a shared troubleshooting tool needs. We are proud we explored a practical use for remote interaction even though the integrated flow remained unfinished.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned the basics of MSS, PyAutoGUI, and handling image frames, along with how much network timing affects an interactive session. ChatGPT helped us shape the scope, while Claude and Copilot offered code suggestions that still needed careful review.
submission.whats_next: We would first connect capture, viewing, and input in one stable local-network session, then measure and reduce delay. After that, we would consider audio and remote connections beyond the same Wi-Fi network.
